facts.label: Readiness view
facts.text: The pack supports a creditor snapshot of OLIN Corp (the Virginia registrant Olin Corporation and its consolidated subsidiaries, a single reporting perimeter) at Q3 2026, with limitations, and no consumer is blocked. The filed 10-K and three 10-Qs are original authority for statements, notes, debt, liquidity and segment facts, while the three Exhibit 99.1 releases are attributed management claims that carry the non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA and net debt ratio. Evidence runs from covenant relief narrative (10-Q Q3 page:13, page:50) to a source risk: the numeric maintenance levels, the executed credit agreements and the October 27, 2026 amendments are exhibits incorporated by reference and not supplied, so covenant headroom and the combined-company facility terms rest on summary text. The downstream consequence is that leverage and liquidity can be computed from printed inputs but a covenant-compliance conclusion cannot be tested. Pinned sources contain no Huntsman financials, so only Olin-side merger facts are supported. Readiness for each consumer is set out in the tables below.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: OLIN Corp, a vertically integrated chlor alkali, epoxy and ammunition manufacturer, ends Q3 2026 with weaker credit metrics than at FY2025, while liquidity remains adequate and the debt stack has no maturity before the receivables facility in November 2027. The strongest support is liquidity: cash of USD 214.8 million plus USD 1,029.6 million undrawn on the revolver, and a revolver and term loan maturity of March 14, 2030 (10-Q Q3 page:13). The weakest point is earnings: company-defined trailing twelve month adjusted EBITDA is USD 536.6 million against USD 651.8 million at FY2025 (EX-99.1 Q3 page:11), so reported total debt of USD 3,013.1 million equals 5.62x and net debt equals 5.21x, up from 4.34x and 4.08x. What decides the outcome is fourth quarter 2026 delivery against guidance of USD 80 million to USD 100 million adjusted EBITDA (EX-99.1 Q3 page:2), the covenant relief that ends by September 30, 2027, and whether the Huntsman merger closes in the first quarter of 2027 with the new USD 2,500.0 million facility (10-Q Q3 page:8). Nine month 2026 free cash flow before dividends was negative, and every ratio below uses the company's non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA unless stated.

facts.label: Covenants
facts.text: The Senior Secured Credit Facility has a maximum net leverage ratio (consolidated total debt net of unrestricted cash over EBITDA, excluding receivables financing borrowings up to USD 425.0 million) and a minimum coverage ratio (EBITDA to interest expense) (10-Q Q3 page:14). The February 19, 2026 amendment relaxed both and adjusted the EBITDA and debt definitions for the covenant relief period, which ends on the earlier of September 30, 2027 and Olin's election, when guarantees and liens fall away (10-K page:140, page:141; 10-Q Q3 page:13). facts.label: Pricing and volume drivers
facts.text: Operating model prioritises Electrochemical Unit margins over sales volumes (Management Language; 10-Q Q3 page:56). Nine month 2026 Chlor Alkali segment income fell USD 190.6 million, driven by the Freeport outage (72.2), lower volumes (55.3), lower pricing (42.0), a legacy litigation charge (36.1), raw materials (32.1) and a smaller 45V tax credit (12.1), partly offset by lower operating costs (59.2) (Documentary Fact; 10-Q Q3 page:41)
facts.basis: Literal handoff table; no financial reinterpretation.

facts.label: Cost structure
facts.text: Electricity is the largest raw material in chlor alkali, about 76% from natural gas or hydroelectric sources; about 73% of salt is internal; ethylene is supplied under a long-term arrangement (Documentary Fact; 10-K page:6). Epoxy inputs are chlorine, caustic soda, cumene, propylene and aromatics (10-K page:9). Winchester buys copper-based strip, lead and propellant under multi-year contracts at conversion charges over exchange metal prices (10-K page:12). Raw materials and utilities purchase commitments were USD 5,559.4 million at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:69)
facts.basis: Literal handoff table; no financial reinterpretation.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: OLIN Corp is a publicly listed, sponsor-free manufacturer whose creditor case rests on integrated chlor alkali and epoxy assets plus a defence-linked ammunition business, and whose near-term outcome is set by a single pending transaction: an all-stock merger of equals with Huntsman Corporation, expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. The strongest support is diversification and integration, with three segments, no customer above 10 percent of 2025 sales and a captive chlorine outlet through epoxy and chlorinated organics. The weakest point is the Chlor Alkali Products and Vinyls segment, where the Freeport vinyl chloride monomer outage cut segment income to USD 80.2 million for the nine months from USD 270.8 million. What decides the credit is whether the merger closes, what the combined company borrows under the new USD 2,500.0 million facility, and whether fourth quarter 2026 earnings meet the USD 80 million to USD 100 million guidance, so execution risk on the merger is the main swing factor.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: On June 15, 2026 Olin entered into a definitive agreement with Huntsman Corporation for an all-stock merger of equals to form OlinHuntsman Corporation; each Huntsman share converts into 0.5476 Olin shares, and Olin holders are expected to own approximately 54.5% and Huntsman holders approximately 45.5% of the combined company (10-Q Q3 page:7, page:8). Shareholders of both companies approved the proposals on August 25, 2026 and the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period expired, but remaining regulatory approvals and customary conditions are outstanding and closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027, having been expected in the first half of 2027 in the July release (10-Q Q3 page:8; EX-99.1 Q2 page:3). The registration statement on Form S-4/A was declared effective on July 13, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:58). Olin could owe a termination fee of USD 121 million, and the Q2 2026 10-Q adds reimbursement of Huntsman expenses of up to USD 30 million (10-Q Q2 page:56). Olin booked acquisition-related costs of USD 13.7 million in Q3 2026 and USD 24.3 million in the nine months and expects USD 35 million to USD 40 million for 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:45). The merger agreement restricts certain Olin actions without Huntsman's consent before closing (10-Q Q3 page:57).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The new debt is the OlinHuntsman Credit Facility of USD 2,500.0 million under a second amendment dated October 27, 2026 to Olin's credit agreement, effective on the merger Closing Date subject to closing and customary conditions. It has a term loan of USD 750.0 million replacing Olin's existing USD 650.0 million term loan facility, and a revolver of USD 1,750.0 million replacing Olin's USD 1,200.0 million revolver and Huntsman's revolver. The term loan amortises at 1.250% per quarter from the first full fiscal quarter after closing through the fourth anniversary quarter, then 1.875% per quarter, and the facility matures five years after the Closing Date. facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: OLIN Corp's fundamental credit is weakening but not impaired in the near term: leverage has stepped up while liquidity and the maturity profile give time to reach the Huntsman merger decision point. The strongest support is USD 1,244.4 million of cash and undrawn revolver, no maturity before the USD 465.0 million receivables facility in November 2027, and three segments that do not move together. The weakest point is trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 536.6 million, which puts net debt to adjusted EBITDA at 5.21x against 4.08x at FY2025 and cash interest cover at 3.15x. What decides the outcome is fourth quarter 2026 delivery against guidance of USD 80 million to USD 100 million, closing of the merger in the first quarter of 2027, and the end of covenant relief by September 30, 2027. Confidence is Medium.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, leverage has risen while earnings fell. Trailing twelve month adjusted EBITDA fell by USD 115.2 million to USD 536.6 million between FY2025 and Q3 2026 (a fall of 17.7 percent), while reported total debt rose by USD 185.8 million to USD 3,013.1 million and cash rose by USD 47.2 million, so net debt rose by USD 138.6 million to USD 2,798.3 million. Net debt to adjusted EBITDA moved from 4.08x to 5.21x, total debt to adjusted EBITDA from 4.34x to 5.62x and cash interest cover from 3.66x to 3.15x (Documentary Fact; CP-1 handoff). The mechanism is that fixed interest and capital costs are carried by a smaller EBITDA base, and the implication is less tolerance for further operating shocks before covenant relief ends. The ratios use the company's non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA, which excludes restructuring, acquisition-related costs, the legacy litigation charge of the first quarter of 2026 and, on the CP-1 reproduction, the FY2025 Shintech charge; the covenant ratio is defined differently and its levels are not supplied.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Second, the earnings decline is concentrated in Chlor Alkali Products and Vinyls. Segment income for the nine months of 2026 was USD 80.2 million against USD 270.8 million, with the Freeport vinyl chloride monomer outage costing USD 72.2 million, lower volumes USD 55.3 million, lower pricing USD 42.0 million and a legacy litigation charge USD 36.1 million, partly offset by USD 59.2 million of lower operating costs (Documentary Fact; CP-1A handoff). Winchester segment income was USD 77.1 million and Epoxy USD 13.7 million for the nine months, against USD 67.1 million and a loss of USD 84.3 million a year earlier. The mechanism is operating leverage in a commodity chlor alkali segment that holds most of the depreciation base; the implication is that recovery of credit metrics depends on that segment normalising after the outage, which management says is restored (Management Language), and on epoxy demand, which the filing describes as weak.

facts.text: Third, cash generation is uneven. Nine month operating cash flow of USD 69.7 million did not cover capital spending of USD 106.6 million, leaving free cash flow before dividends of USD -36.9 million and, after dividends of USD 68.3 million, USD -105.2 million. Trailing twelve month free cash flow was USD 221.5 million, or USD 130.4 million after trailing dividends of USD 91.1 million, because the fourth quarter of 2025 alone produced USD 321.2 million of operating cash flow (Documentary Fact; derived from CP-1 handoff). The mechanism is working capital and timing: receivables rose USD 133.4 million on third quarter sales timing. The implication is that fourth quarter 2026 working capital release, not earnings alone, determines whether net debt falls by year end.

facts.text: Fourth, liquidity is adequate and maturities are not near. Cash of USD 214.8 million plus USD 1,029.6 million undrawn revolver gives USD 1,244.4 million, equal to 2.68 times the USD 465.0 million receivables facility maturing November 19, 2027, the first maturity. The revolver and term loan mature March 14, 2030 and no covenant limited borrowing at September 30, 2026 (CP-1 handoff). facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Fifth, covenant relief and ranking mechanics are time-limited. The February 19, 2026 amendment relaxed the net leverage and coverage covenants, added subsidiary guarantees and collateral for the bank facilities, and limits debt, non-regular distributions and asset sales until the earlier of September 30, 2027 and Olin's election, when guarantees and liens fall away (CP-1 handoff; CP-1A handoff). Numeric levels are not supplied, so headroom is not calculable. The mechanism is that bank debt of USD 1,163.1 million (38.4 percent of principal, comprising the term loan, drawn revolver and receivables facility) has collateral or receivables security during relief, while the senior notes of USD 1,784.6 million (58.9 percent) have security not stated in the pack; the implication is that creditor priority changes when relief ends, and the notes' position cannot be assessed without the indentures. This is a mechanic, not a recovery conclusion.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Sixth, the Huntsman merger replaces uncertainty with a different one. The all-stock merger is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, with a new USD 2,500.0 million facility replacing Olin's bank facilities and Huntsman's revolver (Documentary Fact; CP-1A handoff). The mechanism is a reset of covenants, collateral, amortisation and pricing, with Huntsman obligations joining the guarantor group; the implication is that existing Olin creditors will hold claims on a combined company whose leverage cannot be computed because Huntsman financials, debt and synergy targets are not in the pack. Ratings reflect this: Fitch BB+ on Rating Watch Positive, S&P BB on Credit Watch Developing and Moody's Ba2 with a Negative outlook.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Liquidity runway is the first strength (Documentary Fact): USD 1,244.4 million of cash and undrawn revolver against a nearest maturity of USD 465.0 million, with no covenant restricting borrowing at September 30, 2026. Business diversification is the second (Documentary Fact; CP-1A handoff): three segments, no customer above 10 percent of 2025 sales, a captive chlorine outlet through epoxy and chlorinated organics, and a Winchester business with government contract revenue of about 13 percent of 2025 sales that improved to USD 77.1 million of segment income over the nine months. Third, covenant relief was obtained in February 2026 with the revolver and term loan maturity of March 14, 2030 maintained, and Olin reports compliance with no event of default (Documentary Fact). Fourth, issuer behaviour shows no creditor-adverse transfer: there were no buybacks in the nine months of 2026 after USD 50.5 million in 2025 and no priming or collateral release is documented, though the pack is limited (Analyst Interpretation). Fifth, structural cost actions are cited by management as lowering operating costs, and the nine month Chlor Alkali bridge shows USD 59.2 million of lower operating costs (Management Language qualified by Documentary Fact).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Leverage is elevated and rising: net debt to adjusted EBITDA of 5.21x and total debt to adjusted EBITDA of 5.62x, with cover at 3.15x (Documentary Fact). Earnings are concentrated in a segment hit by an operating outage and by weaker pricing and volumes, and the outage impact in the third quarter of USD 32.1 million exceeded the July estimate of about USD 20 million (Documentary Fact). Epoxy remains challenged by subsidised Asian competition and weak demand (Documentary Fact). Free cash flow for the nine months was negative while the USD 0.20 quarterly dividend was maintained, so dividends of USD 68.3 million were covered by net borrowing (Analyst Interpretation). Ratings were lowered in February 2026 to BB+, Ba2 and BB and now carry mixed watch and outlook signals (Documentary Fact). Fourth quarter guidance of USD 80 million to USD 100 million implies a seasonally weak quarter, with management citing destocking, higher feedstock costs, Asian export pressure and turnarounds (Management Language). Finally, the credit depends on covenant levels, ranking and merger terms that the pack does not contain (Insufficient Information).

spans.text: ## Request

Source readiness for OLIN Corp (issuer id oln, NYSE: OLN), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, current period Q3 2026 (quarter ended September 30, 2026) against FY2025, reporting currency USD, evidence cutoff 2026-11-05. The question is whether the seven pinned filings and releases can support the requested downstream modules (CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2, CP-5) and what remains blocked. This module gives no credit conclusion and calculates nothing.
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on
| Source name | Document family and period | sha256 |
| 10-K_2025-12-31_oln-20251231.htm.jsonl | Form 10-K, fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (150 pages) | 4c4aa24234dd70c75f25e45010299b0359519fd53db6b33485bc189c79880655 |

| EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exhibit991q32026earningspr.htm.jsonl | Exhibit 99.1 earnings release for Q3 2026, dated October 29, 2026 (11 pages) | 27ebe9b3524b1cfc010f76a20b291e6a4f5bd41b4c9d2abf5a2ffd63c041424f |
### Settings source (not issuer evidence)
| Source name | Role | sha256 |

| context | User settings for this run: as-of and cutoff 2026-11-05, current period q3-2026, prior period fy-2025, USD; no deal terms, quotes, ratings, peers or research questions entered | 09d8a3ab70b39856c937eb920b788157e416ce636cea1515d7a99dd15e9d89b1 |
### Supplied handoffs
None. This is the first module of the run and no upstream handoff exists.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven filings and releases are enough for a creditor snapshot of OLIN Corp as of Q3 2026, with stated limits. Debt, liquidity, segments, the pending Huntsman merger and the covenant structure can be traced to filed text. | Medium | The credit agreements, indentures, merger agreement and the numeric covenant levels are not in the pack, so covenant headroom cannot be tested. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The annual filing and three quarterly filings are present, and the latest quarter agrees with its release on the figures checked. | Extraction can rest on filings, with releases used as management claims. | High |
| Covenant relief terms and the new combined-company facility are described in narrative only. | Headroom and post-merger structure cannot be tested against executed terms. | Medium |

| Merger timing moved from first half of 2027 in July to first quarter 2027 in October. | The post-merger credit profile remains conditional on closing and on Huntsman evidence not supplied. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The pack supports a creditor snapshot of OLIN Corp (the Virginia registrant Olin Corporation and its consolidated subsidiaries, a single reporting perimeter) at Q3 2026, with limitations, and no consumer is blocked. The filed 10-K and three 10-Qs are original authority for statements, notes, debt, liquidity and segment facts, while the three Exhibit 99.1 releases are attributed management claims that carry the non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA and net debt ratio. Evidence runs from covenant relief narrative (10-Q Q3 page:13, page:50) to a source risk: the numeric maintenance levels, the executed credit agreements and the October 27, 2026 amendments are exhibits incorporated by reference and not supplied, so covenant headroom and the combined-company facility terms rest on summary text. The downstream consequence is that leverage and liquidity can be computed from printed inputs but a covenant-compliance conclusion cannot be tested. Pinned sources contain no Huntsman financials, so only Olin-side merger facts are supported. Readiness for each consumer is set out in the tables below.
### Source coverage and document assessment
| Source | Original authority and perimeter | Period and basis | Version relationship |

| 10-K FY2025 | Filed annual report, audited by KPMG LLP (page:140); Olin Corporation consolidated; carries the annual debt maturity table (page:108) and, in Item 9B, the February 19, 2026 credit amendments (page:140, page:141) | FY2025, USD millions | Base annual source; its Item 9B describes the First Amendment to the Credit Agreement dated March 14, 2025 |
| 10-Q Q1 2026 | Filed interim report, unaudited; consolidated | Q1 2026 with comparatives | Separate active source, not superseded by later 10-Qs |
| 10-Q Q2 2026 | Filed interim report, unaudited; consolidated; first filing after merger agreement of June 15, 2026 | Q2 2026 and six months | Separate active source |

| 10-Q Q3 2026 | Filed interim report, unaudited; consolidated; latest balance sheet at September 30, 2026 (page:2 to page:5), debt note (page:12 to page:15), liquidity (page:47 to page:52) | Q3 2026 and nine months; comparatives September 30, 2025 and December 31, 2025 | Controlling source for latest period facts; subsequent event of October 27, 2026 (page:8, page:34) |
| EX-99.1 Q1 2026 | Management earnings release; attributed claims | Q1 2026, adjusted EBITDA reconciliation | Supporting only; does not override the 10-Q |
| EX-99.1 Q2 2026 | Management earnings release; attributed claims | Q2 2026 | Supporting only |

| EX-99.1 Q3 2026 | Management earnings release; attributed claims (page:1 to page:3, page:10, page:11) | Q3 2026, nine months and trailing twelve months | Supporting only; carries fourth quarter 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance and the net debt ratio |
### Entity and instrument roles evidenced

Olin Corporation is the only issuer and registrant. Guarantors of the Senior Secured Credit Facility are certain domestic subsidiaries, not named, with covenant-relief-period release of guarantees and liens (10-Q Q3 page:13). Blue Cube Operations LLC is a wholly owned subsidiary named as a litigant (10-Q Q3 page:25). Olin Winchester, LLC is a party to the Fifteenth Amendment of the Amended and Restated Credit and Funding Agreement (10-Q Q3 page:60). Huntsman Corporation is the merger counterparty, not an obligor. Which subsidiaries are guarantors and the restricted perimeter of the covenant EBITDA are unresolved and carried as gaps.
### Strongest contrary evidence and limitations

The releases report adjusted EBITDA on a non-GAAP basis and a net debt ratio that differ in definition from the covenant net leverage ratio, which nets only unrestricted cash and excludes receivables financing up to a stated cap (10-Q Q3 page:14); the two cannot be treated as one measure. Quarter versus nine-month distinctions are printed for the statements (10-Q Q3 page:3) and the reconciliation (EX-99.1 Q3 page:10). On the latest quarter, sales, net income and cash agree between the release (EX-99.1 Q3 page:1, page:3) and the 10-Q (page:3, page:2); only these were compared and nothing was reconciled. Management statements about merger timing and synergies are claims, not facts.
### Consumer readiness
| Consumer | Status | Evidence demand and carried limitations |

| CP-1 financial and debt extraction | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Statements, debt table, facility terms and quarter versus year-to-date figures are in filed text; covenant levels are not printed and variable-rate spreads and pricing grid levels are not printed (searched SOFR and basis points across all sources); the annual maturity table is in the 10-K (page:108) and is dated December 31, 2025 |

| CP-1A business and transaction context | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business, segments and the Huntsman merger terms are in the 10-Q Q3 notes; the Merger Agreement, joint proxy and Huntsman financials are not supplied |
| CP-2 fundamental credit synthesis | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Depends on upstream registers; source evidence for operations, liquidity and ratings is adequate; no market quotes or peers in context |
| CP-5 evidence trace validation | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Can trace claims to the pinned pages; cannot verify claims about documents not supplied |
## Calculations

None. The method prohibits normalization, reconciliation or new calculation in this module; no figure was derived. Every number above is quoted from a source page. Figures that disagree in definition, such as the net debt ratio of the release and the covenant net leverage ratio, are flagged, not reconciled.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation |

| Numeric maintenance covenant levels (net leverage ceiling and interest coverage floor, during and after the relief period) are not printed. Searched covenant, leverage ratio, coverage ratio and relief period across all seven sources; only narrative found (10-K page:140, page:141; 10-Q Q3 page:13, page:14). | High | CP-1, CP-2, CP-5 | Supply the executed Credit Agreement and the 10-K exhibit 10.31 amendment |

| Executed legal documents are not in the pack: the Credit Agreement of March 14, 2025, the First Amendment, the October 27, 2026 second amendment (OlinHuntsman Credit Facility), the Fifteenth Amendment to the PNC agreement, indentures for the notes, the receivables financing agreement and the Merger Agreement. Referenced as exhibits (10-Q Q3 page:60). | High | CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply from EDGAR exhibits; until then legal terms rest on summary text |
| No Huntsman financial statements, joint proxy or S-4; combined-company leverage cannot be assessed. | Medium | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply Huntsman filings and the S-4 if a pro forma view is required |

| Credit ratings are printed only as a table of the three agencies at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:52, page:53); no agency reports and no ratings in the context. | Low | CP-2 | Supply agency reports if rating drivers are needed |

| No investor presentations are supplied; the pack has earnings releases only, which carry no slide or chart content. Image and chart content is not claimed as inspected. | Low | CP-1A | Supply decks if needed |
| Guarantor identity and the restricted perimeter for covenant EBITDA are not stated. | Medium | CP-1, CP-2 | Supply credit agreement definitions |

| Conflict check: Q2 release states merger completion is expected in the first half of 2027 (EX-99.1 Q2 page:3) and the Q3 release and 10-Q state the first quarter of 2027 (EX-99.1 Q3 page:1; 10-Q Q3 page:8). Treated as a dated update, latest controls. The 10-Q says the agreement was entered into June 15, 2026 and the releases say it was announced June 16, 2026; not a conflict. | Low | CP-1A, CP-2 | Use the latest dated statement and label earlier ones |

| Extraction fidelity: text extraction of tables flattens columns; figures must be checked against the printed totals. No fidelity review of the extraction has been done. | Low | All | Keep checks of totals in downstream modules |

Currency is USD in millions throughout, with share data in millions and per-share data in dollars (10-Q Q3 page:2). All statements are unaudited interim except the 10-K. No source is a draft; the 10-Q Q3 is signed October 30, 2026, inside the cutoff. Nothing after 2026-11-05 is used.
## Next module

Proceed to CP-1 with the 10-K and the 10-Q Q3 as controlling sources, using the three releases only as attributed management claims. Carry forward: covenant levels not printed, executed legal documents not supplied, no Huntsman evidence, and the definitional difference between the release net debt ratio and the covenant ratio. Next evidence action: obtain the executed Credit Agreement and amendments if a covenant headroom test is required.

### Financial base view

OLIN Corp, a vertically integrated chlor alkali, epoxy and ammunition manufacturer, ends Q3 2026 with weaker credit metrics than at FY2025, while liquidity remains adequate and the debt stack has no maturity before the receivables facility in November 2027. The strongest support is liquidity: cash of USD 214.8 million plus USD 1,029.6 million undrawn on the revolver, and a revolver and term loan maturity of March 14, 2030 (10-Q Q3 page:13). The weakest point is earnings: company-defined trailing twelve month adjusted EBITDA is USD 536.6 million against USD 651.8 million at FY2025 (EX-99.1 Q3 page:11), so reported total debt of USD 3,013.1 million equals 5.62x and net debt equals 5.21x, up from 4.34x and 4.08x. What decides the outcome is fourth quarter 2026 delivery against guidance of USD 80 million to USD 100 million adjusted EBITDA (EX-99.1 Q3 page:2), the covenant relief that ends by September 30, 2027, and whether the Huntsman merger closes in the first quarter of 2027 with the new USD 2,500.0 million facility (10-Q Q3 page:8). Nine month 2026 free cash flow before dividends was negative, and every ratio below uses the company's non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA unless stated.

### Liquidity

Liquidity at September 30, 2026 is cash of USD 214.8 million (10-Q Q3 page:2) plus revolver undrawn commitments of USD 1,029.6 million, which are net of USD 170.0 million drawn and USD 0.4 million of letters of credit on a USD 1,200.0 million facility (10-Q Q3 page:13), giving USD 1,244.4 million. The 2024 Receivables Financing Agreement adds USD 34.0 million of borrowing-base-limited capacity (10-Q Q3 page:15), giving USD 1,278.4 million, consistent with the release's approximately USD 1.3 billion (EX-99.1 Q3 page:3). No covenant limited borrowing at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:14). At December 31, 2025 the leverage covenant limited additional borrowings to USD 825.3 million (10-K page:65). No facility expires within twelve months of September 30, 2026; the receivables facility matures November 19, 2027, so the USD 465.0 million drawn would fall within twelve months of the December 31, 2026 balance sheet date and could then be classified as current unless extended; the filings do not state the classification.
### Covenants

The Senior Secured Credit Facility has a maximum net leverage ratio (consolidated total debt net of unrestricted cash over EBITDA, excluding receivables financing borrowings up to USD 425.0 million) and a minimum coverage ratio (EBITDA to interest expense) (10-Q Q3 page:14). The February 19, 2026 amendment relaxed both and adjusted the EBITDA and debt definitions for the covenant relief period, which ends on the earlier of September 30, 2027 and Olin's election, when guarantees and liens fall away (10-K page:140, page:141; 10-Q Q3 page:13). The numeric levels, step-downs and the covenant EBITDA are Not supplied after search of all seven sources, so headroom is Not calculable. Olin states it was in compliance with all covenants at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:14). The filings word the leverage test differently: the 10-K describes secured debt (10-K page:106) while the 10-Q describes consolidated total debt, net of unrestricted cash; the executed agreement would settle this. The company ratio of 5.2x (net debt to adjusted EBITDA, all debt) is not the covenant ratio, because the covenant nets only unrestricted cash and excludes up to USD 425.0 million of receivables financing. An illustrative figure on that definition, using reported debt and company adjusted EBITDA (not the covenant EBITDA), is 4.42x (Calculations). The incoming OlinHuntsman Credit Facility will carry a secured debt to EBITDA and a coverage covenant (10-Q Q3 page:8, page:9); levels Not supplied.
### Latest quarter and subsequent events

- Q3 2026 sales were USD 1,747.7 million against USD 1,713.2 million in Q3 2025; adjusted EBITDA was USD 191.4 million against USD 222.4 million (EX-99.1 Q3 page:1). Chlor Alkali Products and Vinyls segment income fell to USD 71.3 million from USD 127.6 million, including USD 32.1 million from the Freeport, TX vinyl chloride monomer plant operating issues and a 45V tax credit benefit of USD 5.0 million against USD 32.0 million (10-Q Q3 page:41; EX-99.1 Q3 page:2). Epoxy returned to USD 0.6 million from a USD 32.2 million loss and Winchester rose to USD 33.8 million from USD 19.3 million (10-Q Q3 page:40).

- Merger: Olin entered into the Huntsman all-stock merger agreement on June 15, 2026; shareholders of both approved on August 25, 2026; the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period expired; closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027, previously the first half of 2027 (10-Q Q3 page:7, page:8; EX-99.1 Q2 page:3). Acquisition-related costs were USD 13.7 million in Q3 2026 and USD 24.3 million in the nine months; USD 35 million to USD 40 million is expected for 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:45).

- Financing: second amendment dated October 27, 2026 to the credit agreement, and a Fifteenth Amendment to the PNC-agented funding agreement of the same date (10-Q Q3 page:34, page:60). Both are subsequent events to the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and are filed by reference only.

- Ratings at September 30, 2026: Fitch BB+ on Rating Watch Positive, Moody's Ba2 Negative, S&P BB on Credit Watch Developing (10-Q Q3 page:52, page:53). In February 2026 Fitch downgraded to BB+ from BBB-, Moody's to Ba2 from Ba1 and S&P to BB from BB+ (10-Q Q1 page:43).

- Fourth quarter 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance is USD 80 million to USD 100 million, with lower results expected from elevated customer destocking, higher feedstock costs, Asian export pressure and planned turnarounds (EX-99.1 Q3 page:2; 10-Q Q3 page:45). Full year 2026 capital spending is about USD 200 million and depreciation and amortization about USD 470 million (10-Q Q3 page:45).
- No share repurchases in 2026; USD 1,948.9 million remained authorized (10-Q Q3 page:59). The quarterly dividend stayed at USD 0.20 per share (10-Q Q3 page:4).

## Calculations
Trailing twelve month (LTM) amounts equal nine month 2026 plus FY2025 less nine month 2025 unless stated; the same pattern holds at Q1 and Q2.

- LTM sales: 5,072.6 + 6,780.8 - 5,115.7 = 6,737.7. LTM gross margin: 418.7 + 501.5 - 470.2 = 450.0. LTM operating income: 27.4 + 5.3 - 161.8 = -129.1. LTM net income attributable: -81.9 + -100.5 - 42.9 = -225.3. LTM depreciation and amortization: 353.7 + 521.6 - 395.9 = 479.4. LTM interest expense, net: 130.9 + 183.9 - 138.1 = 176.7.
- FY2025 interest expense, net: 188.3 - 4.4 = 183.9 (10-K page:81).

- FY2025 EBITDA before add-backs, on the release definition (net income plus interest, taxes, D&A): -101.1 + 183.9 + (-60.0) + 521.6 = 544.4. Cross-check to the printed FY2025 adjusted EBITDA: 544.4 + restructuring 33.4 + Shintech charge 75.0 - environmental recovery 1.0 = 651.8, equal to the figure in the releases (EX-99.1 Q3 page:11; restructuring from 10-K page:81, the Shintech charge from 10-Q Q3 page:25, the recovery from EX-99.1 Q3 page:10, where it is shown for the nine months of 2025). The exact tie suggests these were the only FY2025 add-backs, but the FY2025 add-back schedule itself is not in the pack.
- LTM EBITDA before add-backs: 387.2 + 544.4 - 570.8 = 360.8.

- Interest cover (adjusted EBITDA / cash interest): FY2025 651.8 / 177.9 = 3.66x; Q1 552.4 / 160.7 = 3.44x; Q2 567.6 / 171.1 = 3.32x; Q3 536.6 / 170.2 = 3.15x. Using interest expense, net rather than cash interest, Q3 LTM cover is 536.6 / 176.7 = 3.04x.

- Cash flow: Q3 stand-alone operating cash flow 69.7 - (-40.7) = 110.4; Q3 2025 153.0 - 126.3 = 26.7 (10-Q Q2 page:4). Q3 stand-alone capital expenditures 106.6 - 72.7 = 33.9; Q3 2025 163.5 - 92.4 = 71.1. Free cash flow before dividends: Q3 2026 110.4 - 33.9 = 76.5; Q3 2025 26.7 - 71.1 = -44.4; nine months 2026 69.7 - 106.6 = -36.9; nine months 2025 153.0 - 163.5 = -10.5; FY2025 474.2 - 226.3 = 247.9; LTM operating cash flow 69.7 + 474.2 - 153.0 = 390.9, LTM capital expenditures 106.6 + 226.3 - 163.5 = 169.4, LTM free cash flow 390.9 - 169.4 = 221.5. LTM dividends: 68.3 + 91.6 - 68.8 = 91.1. Nine month free cash flow after dividends: -36.9 - 68.3 = -105.2.

- Liquidity: Q3 214.8 + 1,029.6 = 1,244.4; plus receivables capacity 34.0 = 1,278.4. Q1 192.2 + 1,039.6 = 1,231.8. Q2 177.4 + 989.6 = 1,167.0. FY2025 undrawn revolver 1,200.0 - 0.0 - 0.4 = 1,199.6, so cash plus undrawn 167.6 + 1,199.6 = 1,367.2, against the covenant-limited additional borrowing of 825.3. Revolver check at Q3: 1,200.0 - 170.0 - 0.4 = 1,029.6, equal to the printed figure.

- Illustrative covenant-style leverage: (3,013.1 - 214.8 - 425.0) / 536.6 = 2,373.3 / 536.6 = 4.42x, using reported debt net of deferred costs, all cash as unrestricted, the full 425.0 receivables exclusion (the drawn 465.0 exceeds the cap) and company adjusted EBITDA. This is not the covenant calculation.
- Guidance-implied FY2026 adjusted EBITDA: 468.9 + 80 = 548.9 to 468.9 + 100 = 568.9, a forward figure that depends on meeting guidance.
- Implied Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA: 651.8 - 584.1 = 67.7.
- Operating lease liabilities: 72.7 + 315.1 = 387.8 at September 30, 2026.

Proceed to CP-1A with this handoff: carry forward that adjusted EBITDA is management non-GAAP, that covenant levels are not supplied, the February 2026 rating downgrades and September 2026 watch status, the November 19, 2027 receivables maturity, and the conditional OlinHuntsman facility. Business, ownership and transaction context for OLIN Corp (Olin Corporation, NYSE: OLN), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, current period Q3 2026 against FY2025, reporting currency USD. Scope: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to a creditor, the pending Huntsman merger and its new credit facility, issuer-level governance and capital allocation behaviour, and a dated timeline to the 2026-11-05 cutoff. Figures repeat the accepted financial handoff exactly.

## Findings

### Business and transaction view

OLIN Corp is a publicly listed, sponsor-free manufacturer whose creditor case rests on integrated chlor alkali and epoxy assets plus a defence-linked ammunition business, and whose near-term outcome is set by a single pending transaction: an all-stock merger of equals with Huntsman Corporation, expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. The strongest support is diversification and integration, with three segments, no customer above 10 percent of 2025 sales and a captive chlorine outlet through epoxy and chlorinated organics. The weakest point is the Chlor Alkali Products and Vinyls segment, where the Freeport vinyl chloride monomer outage cut segment income to USD 80.2 million for the nine months from USD 270.8 million. What decides the credit is whether the merger closes, what the combined company borrows under the new USD 2,500.0 million facility, and whether fourth quarter 2026 earnings meet the USD 80 million to USD 100 million guidance, so execution risk on the merger is the main swing factor.
### Company and operating model
| Item | Value |

| Reporting entity and perimeter | Olin Corporation, a Virginia corporation incorporated in 1892, reporting consolidated with its subsidiaries; guarantor subsidiaries are not named (Documentary Fact; 10-Q Q3 page:6, page:13) |

| Business description | "A leading vertically integrated global manufacturer and distributor of chemical products and a leading U.S. manufacturer of ammunition" is the company's own description (Management Language; 10-K page:4) |

| Segments and mix | Chlor Alkali Products and Vinyls 54%, Epoxy 20% and Winchester 26% of 2025 sales per the 10-K (Documentary Fact; 10-K page:4); nine months 2026 sales were 2,427.2, 1,189.9 and 1,455.5 of 5,072.6 (47.8%, 23.5% and 28.7%, derived; 10-Q Q3 page:23) |

| Revenue model | Industrial and commercial users and distributors; epoxy resins, caustic soda and sporting ammunition sold to many users, chlorine and chlorinated organics in substantial quantities to a relatively small number; no single customer above 10% of 2025 sales; U.S. government agencies about 13% of 2025 sales (Documentary Fact; 10-K page:13) |

| Pricing and volume drivers | Operating model prioritises Electrochemical Unit margins over sales volumes (Management Language; 10-Q Q3 page:56). Nine month 2026 Chlor Alkali segment income fell USD 190.6 million, driven by the Freeport outage (72.2), lower volumes (55.3), lower pricing (42.0), a legacy litigation charge (36.1), raw materials (32.1) and a smaller 45V tax credit (12.1), partly offset by lower operating costs (59.2) (Documentary Fact; 10-Q Q3 page:41) |

| Cost structure | Electricity is the largest raw material in chlor alkali, about 76% from natural gas or hydroelectric sources; about 73% of salt is internal; ethylene is supplied under a long-term arrangement (Documentary Fact; 10-K page:6). Epoxy inputs are chlorine, caustic soda, cumene, propylene and aromatics (10-K page:9). Winchester buys copper-based strip, lead and propellant under multi-year contracts at conversion charges over exchange metal prices (10-K page:12). Raw materials and utilities purchase commitments were USD 5,559.4 million at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:69) |

| Capital spending and depreciation | Management expects 2026 capital spending of about USD 200 million "to maintain our current operating facilities" and depreciation and amortization of about USD 470 million (Management Language; 10-Q Q3 page:45, page:48); nine month capital spending was USD 106.6 million (10-Q Q3 page:4) |

| Working capital | Nine month 2026 working capital increased USD 191.0 million against USD 264.9 million in 2025; receivables rose USD 133.4 million and inventories USD 81.0 million (Documentary Fact; 10-Q Q3 page:48); last-in, first-out reserve USD 203.0 million (10-Q Q3 page:11) |

| Geography | Nine month 2026 sales: United States 3,580.3, Europe 446.0, other foreign 1,046.3 of 5,072.6 (70.6% United States, derived; 10-Q Q3 page:23); Epoxy sold about 59% outside the United States in 2025 (10-K page:13) |

| Winchester contracts | Operates the government-owned Lake City Army Ammunition Plant under a contract of seven years from October 1, 2020 extended by three years, terminable for convenience; the plant is government-owned and contractor-operated; military and law enforcement sales were 887.7 of 1,455.5 in the nine months and over-time revenue 330.0 (Documentary Fact; 10-K page:10, page:13; 10-Q Q3 page:24) |
| Seasonality | Fourth quarter is typically the weakest seasonal quarter (Documentary Fact; 10-Q Q3 page:45) |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

On June 15, 2026 Olin entered into a definitive agreement with Huntsman Corporation for an all-stock merger of equals to form OlinHuntsman Corporation; each Huntsman share converts into 0.5476 Olin shares, and Olin holders are expected to own approximately 54.5% and Huntsman holders approximately 45.5% of the combined company (10-Q Q3 page:7, page:8). Shareholders of both companies approved the proposals on August 25, 2026 and the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period expired, but remaining regulatory approvals and customary conditions are outstanding and closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027, having been expected in the first half of 2027 in the July release (10-Q Q3 page:8; EX-99.1 Q2 page:3). The registration statement on Form S-4/A was declared effective on July 13, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:58). Olin could owe a termination fee of USD 121 million, and the Q2 2026 10-Q adds reimbursement of Huntsman expenses of up to USD 30 million (10-Q Q2 page:56). Olin booked acquisition-related costs of USD 13.7 million in Q3 2026 and USD 24.3 million in the nine months and expects USD 35 million to USD 40 million for 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:45). The merger agreement restricts certain Olin actions without Huntsman's consent before closing (10-Q Q3 page:57).

The new debt is the OlinHuntsman Credit Facility of USD 2,500.0 million under a second amendment dated October 27, 2026 to Olin's credit agreement, effective on the merger Closing Date subject to closing and customary conditions. It has a term loan of USD 750.0 million replacing Olin's existing USD 650.0 million term loan facility, and a revolver of USD 1,750.0 million replacing Olin's USD 1,200.0 million revolver and Huntsman's revolver. The term loan amortises at 1.250% per quarter from the first full fiscal quarter after closing through the fourth anniversary quarter, then 1.875% per quarter, and the facility matures five years after the Closing Date. It is guaranteed by certain Olin subsidiaries and certain Huntsman subsidiaries, secured by first priority liens on certain assets, carries a pricing grid on the net leverage ratio, and has covenants on secured debt to EBITDA and on EBITDA to interest expense, with levels not supplied. The term loan is expected to be fully drawn at closing, with proceeds and any revolver loans used to refinance Olin's senior secured facility, repay and terminate Huntsman's revolver and pay fees (10-Q Q3 page:8, page:9). Olin's senior notes of USD 669.3 million, USD 515.3 million and USD 600.0 million and its USD 465.0 million receivables facility are not stated to be refinanced (CP-1 handoff; 10-Q Q3 page:12). No new notes issuance is described. Huntsman's debt, its balance sheet, its amounts under its revolver and the pro forma capital structure are not in the pack, so combined leverage and the net new debt at closing are not calculable.

### Ownership and capital allocation

Share repurchases were USD 711.3 million in 2023, USD 300.3 million in 2024 and USD 50.5 million in 2025, and nil in the nine months of 2026; USD 1,948.9 million of authorisation remained at September 30, 2026 (10-K page:83; 10-Q Q3 page:4, page:59). Dividends were USD 91.6 million in 2025 and USD 68.3 million in the nine months of 2026 at USD 0.20 per quarter, described as the 398th consecutive quarterly dividend in May 2026 (10-K page:83; EX-99.1 Q1 page:3). Nine month 2026 free cash flow before dividends was USD -36.9 million (CP-1 handoff), so, as an Analyst Interpretation, dividends and the USD 31.3 million Mitsui payment were covered by net long-term debt borrowings of USD 185.3 million (10-Q Q3 page:4). During the covenant relief period the February 2026 amendment limits dividends and distributions beyond regularly scheduled dividends, debt incurrence and certain asset sales (10-K page:141). Acquisitions were modest: AMMO small caliber assets for USD 55.8 million on April 18, 2025 and White Flyer targets for USD 63.5 million on October 1, 2023 (10-Q Q3 page:7; 10-K page:10); acquisition appetite is not inferred from these.

### Credit translations
Evidence, mechanic and implication for the main conclusions:

First, earnings concentration. Evidence: Chlor Alkali Products and Vinyls segment income of USD 80.2 million for nine months 2026 against USD 270.8 million, with the Freeport VCM outage costing USD 72.2 million (10-Q Q3 page:41). Mechanic: the segment carries the largest share of depreciation and amortization (282.4 of 353.7 in nine months 2026, 10-Q Q3 page:23), so volume loss and price weakness flow directly into trailing adjusted EBITDA, which fell to USD 536.6 million. Implication: net debt to adjusted EBITDA rose to 5.21x from 4.08x at FY2025 and cash interest cover fell to 3.15x from 3.66x (CP-1 handoff), narrowing tolerance for further operating shocks. Counter-evidence: Winchester and Epoxy improved, and management guides fourth quarter 2026 adjusted EBITDA of USD 80 million to USD 100 million, which is a management expectation.

Second, merger transition. Evidence: all-stock merger with a new USD 2,500.0 million facility replacing Olin's bank facilities and Huntsman's revolver (10-Q Q3 page:8, page:9). Mechanic: the new term loan of USD 750.0 million is expected to be fully drawn at closing and amortises at 1.250% per quarter, while refinancing resets covenants, collateral and the pricing grid; Huntsman's obligations enter the structure. Implication: refinancing risk for Olin's bank debt is addressed only if the merger closes; the combined leverage and the ranking of existing notes cannot be assessed from this pack, and rating agencies are on watch with different directions (Fitch positive, S&P developing, Moody's negative outlook), which signals uncertainty about the combined credit.

Third, liquidity under relief. Evidence: cash of USD 214.8 million, USD 1,029.6 million undrawn revolver, USD 465.0 million receivables facility maturing November 19, 2027 and covenant relief ending by September 30, 2027 (CP-1 handoff). Mechanic: if the merger does not close, the relief period still ends by September 30, 2027 on current terms and the receivables facility then matures within about two months. Implication: monitoring posture should focus on the merger timetable, fourth quarter earnings and any covenant amendment; the numeric covenant levels are not supplied.

## Calculations
- United States share, nine months 2026: 3,580.3 / 5,072.6 = 70.6%.
- Winchester share of FY2025 sales: 1,724.6 / 6,780.8 = 25.4%, against 26% stated (10-K page:4, page:129).
- Winchester military and law enforcement share, nine months 2026: 887.7 / 1,455.5 = 61.0%.

- Chlor Alkali segment income change, nine months: 80.2 - 270.8 = -190.6, equal to the printed decrease (10-Q Q3 page:41); the listed drivers sum as -72.2 - 55.3 - 42.0 - 36.1 - 32.1 - 12.1 + 59.2 = -190.6.

- Term loan step-up at closing: 750.0 new commitment against 528.1 outstanding on the existing term loan is 221.9 more term debt, if the new term loan is fully drawn and the 528.1 balance is unchanged at closing; Huntsman revolver and other debt are Not supplied, so net new debt is Not calculable.
- Quarterly term loan amortisation on 750.0 assumed fully drawn: 1.250% = 9.375 per quarter, or 37.5 per year; 1.875% = 14.0625 per quarter, or 56.25 per year.
- Lake City contract term implied: seven years from October 1, 2020 ends in 2027, plus three years of extension ends in 2030 (derived from 10-K page:10; exact dates not printed).
- Figures carried from the CP-1 handoff without change: 5.21x, 4.08x, 3.15x, 3.66x, trailing adjusted EBITDA 536.6, free cash flow before dividends -36.9 for nine months 2026.

Amounts are USD millions as reported. Facts after September 30, 2026 are labelled subsequent events. Nothing dated after 2026-11-05 is used as fact; expected closing and contract dates are forward terms.
## Next module

Proceed to CP-2 with this handoff and the CP-1 handoff. Carry forward: earnings concentration in Chlor Alkali Products and Vinyls, the unclosed Huntsman merger and the conditional USD 2,500.0 million facility, relief-period covenants with unsupplied levels, rating watches in different directions, and the four logged conflicts. Do not draw combined-company conclusions without Huntsman evidence.

Fundamental credit synthesis for OLIN Corp (Olin Corporation, NYSE: OLN), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, current period Q3 2026 against FY2025, reporting currency USD millions. The question is what the fundamental credit view is and which strengths, weaknesses, findings and risks drive it, from the accepted financial and business handoffs only. No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion is given.
## Sources
### Issuer sources relied on
This module reads upstream handoffs only and quotes no source text. The issuer sources behind those handoffs, and used here only to confirm locators, are:

| EX-99.1_2026-07-30_exhibit991q22026earningspr.htm.jsonl | 08a70fcc145c266c21d73e09e50eda1490a6994f07dbbc111206ffd51445010c |
| EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exhibit991q32026earningspr.htm.jsonl | 27ebe9b3524b1cfc010f76a20b291e6a4f5bd41b4c9d2abf5a2ffd63c041424f |

No upstream handoff is corrected here. The CP-1A handoff already corrects the CP-0 statement on ratings and adds the Huntsman expense reimbursement of up to USD 30 million to the termination fee.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| OLIN Corp's credit is weakening but near-term liquidity is adequate. Net debt to adjusted EBITDA rose to 5.21x from 4.08x as trailing earnings fell. The Huntsman merger and covenant relief timing decide the next year. | Medium | Covenant levels, Huntsman financials and executed debt documents are not supplied, so headroom and combined leverage cannot be tested. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Trailing adjusted EBITDA fell to USD 536.6 million from USD 651.8 million while total debt rose to USD 3,013.1 million. | Leverage and interest cover both deteriorated, leaving less tolerance for another operating shock. | High |

| Liquidity is USD 1,244.4 million and the first maturity is the USD 465.0 million receivables facility in November 2027. | Near-term refinancing pressure is low, but 2029 and 2030 maturities are heavy. | Medium |

| Nine month free cash flow was USD -36.9 million, while trailing twelve month free cash flow was USD 221.5 million. | Cash generation depends on a strong fourth quarter and working capital timing. | Medium |

| Covenant relief ends no later than September 30, 2027 and the merger is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. | The credit depends on merger execution, new facility terms and unsupplied covenant levels. | Medium |
### Credit view

OLIN Corp's fundamental credit is weakening but not impaired in the near term: leverage has stepped up while liquidity and the maturity profile give time to reach the Huntsman merger decision point. The strongest support is USD 1,244.4 million of cash and undrawn revolver, no maturity before the USD 465.0 million receivables facility in November 2027, and three segments that do not move together. The weakest point is trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 536.6 million, which puts net debt to adjusted EBITDA at 5.21x against 4.08x at FY2025 and cash interest cover at 3.15x. What decides the outcome is fourth quarter 2026 delivery against guidance of USD 80 million to USD 100 million, closing of the merger in the first quarter of 2027, and the end of covenant relief by September 30, 2027. Confidence is Medium.
### Assessment
| Element | Content | Category | Confidence and basis |

| Fundamental credit view | Weakening: elevated leverage and falling cover, adequate near-term liquidity, diversified but cyclical business, material event risk from the merger | Analyst Interpretation | Medium; CP-1 leverage, cover and liquidity figures and the CP-1A segment, merger and governance rows; held below High because CP-1A judges this module ready with limitations and covenant levels are not supplied |

| Thesis | Olin's creditors are supported by liquidity, integration and a defence-linked ammunition business, but are exposed to a concentrated chlor alkali earnings decline, thin cover and an unclosed merger that will reset the capital structure | Analyst Interpretation | Medium; same basis |
### Key findings

First, leverage has risen while earnings fell. Trailing twelve month adjusted EBITDA fell by USD 115.2 million to USD 536.6 million between FY2025 and Q3 2026 (a fall of 17.7 percent), while reported total debt rose by USD 185.8 million to USD 3,013.1 million and cash rose by USD 47.2 million, so net debt rose by USD 138.6 million to USD 2,798.3 million. Net debt to adjusted EBITDA moved from 4.08x to 5.21x, total debt to adjusted EBITDA from 4.34x to 5.62x and cash interest cover from 3.66x to 3.15x (Documentary Fact; CP-1 handoff). The mechanism is that fixed interest and capital costs are carried by a smaller EBITDA base, and the implication is less tolerance for further operating shocks before covenant relief ends. The ratios use the company's non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA, which excludes restructuring, acquisition-related costs, the legacy litigation charge of the first quarter of 2026 and, on the CP-1 reproduction, the FY2025 Shintech charge; the covenant ratio is defined differently and its levels are not supplied.

Second, the earnings decline is concentrated in Chlor Alkali Products and Vinyls. Segment income for the nine months of 2026 was USD 80.2 million against USD 270.8 million, with the Freeport vinyl chloride monomer outage costing USD 72.2 million, lower volumes USD 55.3 million, lower pricing USD 42.0 million and a legacy litigation charge USD 36.1 million, partly offset by USD 59.2 million of lower operating costs (Documentary Fact; CP-1A handoff). Winchester segment income was USD 77.1 million and Epoxy USD 13.7 million for the nine months, against USD 67.1 million and a loss of USD 84.3 million a year earlier. The mechanism is operating leverage in a commodity chlor alkali segment that holds most of the depreciation base; the implication is that recovery of credit metrics depends on that segment normalising after the outage, which management says is restored (Management Language), and on epoxy demand, which the filing describes as weak.

Third, cash generation is uneven. Nine month operating cash flow of USD 69.7 million did not cover capital spending of USD 106.6 million, leaving free cash flow before dividends of USD -36.9 million and, after dividends of USD 68.3 million, USD -105.2 million. Trailing twelve month free cash flow was USD 221.5 million, or USD 130.4 million after trailing dividends of USD 91.1 million, because the fourth quarter of 2025 alone produced USD 321.2 million of operating cash flow (Documentary Fact; derived from CP-1 handoff). The mechanism is working capital and timing: receivables rose USD 133.4 million on third quarter sales timing. The implication is that fourth quarter 2026 working capital release, not earnings alone, determines whether net debt falls by year end.

Fourth, liquidity is adequate and maturities are not near. Cash of USD 214.8 million plus USD 1,029.6 million undrawn revolver gives USD 1,244.4 million, equal to 2.68 times the USD 465.0 million receivables facility maturing November 19, 2027, the first maturity. The revolver and term loan mature March 14, 2030 and no covenant limited borrowing at September 30, 2026 (CP-1 handoff). The mechanism is that the nearest wall is small against liquidity, but the 2029 notes of USD 669.3 million and 2030 maturities of USD 1,213.4 million together are USD 1,882.7 million, or 62.1 percent of USD 3,030.7 million principal. The implication is that refinancing risk sits in 2029 and 2030 and depends on market access.

Fifth, covenant relief and ranking mechanics are time-limited. The February 19, 2026 amendment relaxed the net leverage and coverage covenants, added subsidiary guarantees and collateral for the bank facilities, and limits debt, non-regular distributions and asset sales until the earlier of September 30, 2027 and Olin's election, when guarantees and liens fall away (CP-1 handoff; CP-1A handoff). Numeric levels are not supplied, so headroom is not calculable. The mechanism is that bank debt of USD 1,163.1 million (38.4 percent of principal, comprising the term loan, drawn revolver and receivables facility) has collateral or receivables security during relief, while the senior notes of USD 1,784.6 million (58.9 percent) have security not stated in the pack; the implication is that creditor priority changes when relief ends, and the notes' position cannot be assessed without the indentures. This is a mechanic, not a recovery conclusion.

Sixth, the Huntsman merger replaces uncertainty with a different one. The all-stock merger is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, with a new USD 2,500.0 million facility replacing Olin's bank facilities and Huntsman's revolver (Documentary Fact; CP-1A handoff). The mechanism is a reset of covenants, collateral, amortisation and pricing, with Huntsman obligations joining the guarantor group; the implication is that existing Olin creditors will hold claims on a combined company whose leverage cannot be computed because Huntsman financials, debt and synergy targets are not in the pack. Ratings reflect this: Fitch BB+ on Rating Watch Positive, S&P BB on Credit Watch Developing and Moody's Ba2 with a Negative outlook.

Seventh, claims outside reported debt are moderate but real: operating lease liabilities of USD 387.8 million, an environmental reserve of USD 156.8 million, a net balance sheet pension position of USD 63.6 million (accrued pension liability USD 196.5 million less pension assets USD 132.9 million) with a foreign plan deficit of USD 204.2 million at December 31, 2025, and the Shintech judgment on which about USD 114 million was paid in the nine months (CP-1 handoff). The implication is claims that rank alongside financial debt in cash terms but sit outside the debt ratios.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Liquidity runway is the first strength (Documentary Fact): USD 1,244.4 million of cash and undrawn revolver against a nearest maturity of USD 465.0 million, with no covenant restricting borrowing at September 30, 2026. Business diversification is the second (Documentary Fact; CP-1A handoff): three segments, no customer above 10 percent of 2025 sales, a captive chlorine outlet through epoxy and chlorinated organics, and a Winchester business with government contract revenue of about 13 percent of 2025 sales that improved to USD 77.1 million of segment income over the nine months. Third, covenant relief was obtained in February 2026 with the revolver and term loan maturity of March 14, 2030 maintained, and Olin reports compliance with no event of default (Documentary Fact). Fourth, issuer behaviour shows no creditor-adverse transfer: there were no buybacks in the nine months of 2026 after USD 50.5 million in 2025 and no priming or collateral release is documented, though the pack is limited (Analyst Interpretation). Fifth, structural cost actions are cited by management as lowering operating costs, and the nine month Chlor Alkali bridge shows USD 59.2 million of lower operating costs (Management Language qualified by Documentary Fact).

Weaknesses. Leverage is elevated and rising: net debt to adjusted EBITDA of 5.21x and total debt to adjusted EBITDA of 5.62x, with cover at 3.15x (Documentary Fact). Earnings are concentrated in a segment hit by an operating outage and by weaker pricing and volumes, and the outage impact in the third quarter of USD 32.1 million exceeded the July estimate of about USD 20 million (Documentary Fact). Epoxy remains challenged by subsidised Asian competition and weak demand (Documentary Fact). Free cash flow for the nine months was negative while the USD 0.20 quarterly dividend was maintained, so dividends of USD 68.3 million were covered by net borrowing (Analyst Interpretation). Ratings were lowered in February 2026 to BB+, Ba2 and BB and now carry mixed watch and outlook signals (Documentary Fact). Fourth quarter guidance of USD 80 million to USD 100 million implies a seasonally weak quarter, with management citing destocking, higher feedstock costs, Asian export pressure and turnarounds (Management Language). Finally, the credit depends on covenant levels, ranking and merger terms that the pack does not contain (Insufficient Information).
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Earnings and leverage | Trailing adjusted EBITDA of 536.6 supports total debt of 3,013.1 at 5.62x; a weak fourth quarter lowers the base further | Little cushion before covenant and rating pressure; with net debt unchanged, guidance delivery would still leave net debt to adjusted EBITDA at about 4.92x to 5.10x | Material |

| Covenant relief expiry and untested headroom | Relief ends by September 30, 2027; numeric levels unsupplied | Compliance after relief cannot be verified; bank lenders could reprice or restrict borrowing | Material |

| Merger execution and combined leverage | Closing conditions, regulatory approvals and a USD 2,500.0 million facility reset the structure; Huntsman data absent | Existing creditors face an unquantified combined credit; if the merger fails, the standalone profile described here remains and Olin may owe a termination fee of USD 121 million under specified circumstances | Material |
| Refinancing of 2029 and 2030 maturities | USD 1,882.7 million falls due in 2029 and 2030, 62.1 percent of principal | Dependent on market access and ratings after the merger decision | Material |

| Chlor alkali operating risk | One segment holds the earnings swing and the Freeport plant; the Texas emissions suit is open | Further outages or penalties could extend the earnings fall; amount of penalties Not supplied | Material |

| Receivables facility maturity | USD 465.0 million due November 19, 2027, with USD 34.0 million of further capacity | Falls within twelve months at the December 31, 2026 balance sheet date unless extended | Minor |
| Claims outside debt | Leases, environmental, pension and legal claims sit beside debt | Additional cash calls not in ratios; scale is moderate against liquidity | Minor |
### Gaps ledger
| Gap | Why it matters | Affects | Severity | Action |

| Numeric covenant levels and covenant EBITDA not supplied | Headroom and breach sensitivity cannot be tested | Leverage, liquidity, monitoring posture | High | Obtain the executed credit agreement and amendments |

| Huntsman financials, merger agreement, synergy targets not supplied (CP-1A signal) | Combined leverage and closing risk cannot be assessed | Credit view, merger risk | High | Obtain Huntsman filings, S-4 and the merger agreement |

| Indentures not supplied; security and guarantors of senior notes unknown | Priority of notes against collateralised bank debt cannot be set | Creditor control, loss given default mechanics | High | Obtain indentures |
| CP-1A judges this module ready with limitations (CP-1A signal) | Confidence held below High | All conclusions | Medium | State limits; do not draw combined-company conclusions |

| Adjusted EBITDA is a management non-GAAP measure | Ratios depend on company add-backs; the FY2025 figure was reproduced from filing lines but not from an issued reconciliation | Leverage and cover | Medium | Treat ratios as management basis |
| Floating interest rates for 2026 not stated | Interest cost cannot be rebuilt by instrument | Cover, debt service | Low | Obtain pricing grid |
| Unpaid Shintech balance and Texas penalties unknown | Residual cash calls not calculable | Liquidity | Low | Read litigation filings |
## Calculations
- Adjusted EBITDA decline: 651.8 - 536.6 = 115.2; 115.2 / 651.8 = 17.7 percent.
- Ratio changes: 5.21 - 4.08 = 1.13x net leverage; 5.62 - 4.34 = 1.28x total leverage; 3.66 - 3.15 = 0.51x lower cover.
- Fourth quarter 2025 operating cash flow: 474.2 - 153.0 = 321.2 (10-K page:82; 10-Q Q3 page:4). Fourth quarter 2025 adjusted EBITDA: 651.8 - 584.1 = 67.7.
- Free cash flow: nine months 69.7 - 106.6 = -36.9; after dividends -36.9 - 68.3 = -105.2; trailing twelve months 221.5, or 221.5 - 91.1 = 130.4 after dividends (CP-1 handoff).
- Liquidity coverage of first maturity: 1,244.4 / 465.0 = 2.68x.

- Secured and unsecured mix of principal 3,030.7: term loan 528.1 + revolver 170.0 + receivables 465.0 = 1,163.1, or 38.4 percent; notes 669.3 + 515.3 + 600.0 = 1,784.6, or 58.9 percent; recovery zone bonds 83.0, or 2.7 percent.

- Guidance-implied sensitivity (not a forecast): trailing adjusted EBITDA at December 31, 2026 if the fourth quarter delivers guidance is 468.9 + 80 = 548.9 to 468.9 + 100 = 568.9. With net debt held at the September 30, 2026 level of 2,798.3, net debt to adjusted EBITDA would be 2,798.3 / 548.9 = 5.10x to 2,798.3 / 568.9 = 4.92x. The guidance range is a management expectation and net debt will move with fourth quarter cash flow.
- Capital intensity: trailing adjusted EBITDA less trailing capital expenditures is 536.6 - 169.4 = 367.2; net debt over that is 2,798.3 / 367.2 = 7.62x.
- Net pension position on the balance sheet: 196.5 - 132.9 = 63.6.
## Gaps

The gaps ledger above lists what the synthesis lacks. Inherited limits: the CP-0 handoff records no numeric covenant levels, no executed legal documents and no Huntsman evidence; the CP-1 handoff records the management basis of adjusted EBITDA, unstated 2026 floating rates and an undetermined Shintech balance; the CP-1A handoff records unsupplied merger agreement, Huntsman data, synergy targets, beneficial owners and the change-of-control status of the pension plan. The figures in this module are repeated from the CP-1 handoff without change, and no source dated after 2026-11-05 is used.
## Next module

Proceed to CP-5 to trace each material claim here to its handoff and source page. Points for validation: the 5.21x, 4.08x, 3.15x and 3.66x ratios, liquidity of 1,244.4, the maturity concentration of 62.1 percent and the secured mix of 38.4 percent, the guidance-implied sensitivity range, and the statements that security of the senior notes is not supplied and that the Shintech payment of about USD 114 million was made in the nine months of 2026.

### Evidence trace view

The Olin analysis is traceable enough for a restricted committee read: of 16 material claims traced to filing pages, 6 are directly sourced, 7 are calculated from sourced inputs, 1 is assumption-based, 1 is analyst inference and 1 is a logged conflict. The strongest support is that leverage, cover, liquidity and free cash flow recompute exactly from printed figures. The most important provenance gap is that the numeric covenant levels, indentures, merger agreement and Huntsman data are absent, so covenant compliance, ranking of the senior notes and combined-company credit cannot be traced to anything. The lineage defect that matters next is that trailing adjusted EBITDA is a management non-GAAP measure. Five minor locator errors were found and logged; no figure was wrong. Remediation owner for the critical gap is the document request listed in the gaps ledger.
